The {5, 8} funnel.title: The {5, 8} funnel
The {5, 8} funnel.why: Collatz-type largest-prime-factor map; cycle {5,8} confirmed, but excluding divergent prime-driven climbs is Collatz-hard.

Doubling minus one.title: Doubling minus one
Doubling minus one.why: Composites shrink, primes double (Cunningham chains of 2nd kind); cycles confirmed; no obvious potential function, Collatz-like.

Two long loops.title: Two long loops
Two long loops.why: Cycles through 46 (9) and 80 (7) confirmed; global convergence of mixed P-map is Collatz-type.

Gerver's constant has unbounded partial.title: Gerver's constant has unbounded partial quotients
Gerver's constant has unbounded partial.why: Unbounded partial quotients unknown even for pi; Gerver's constant is defined implicitly, so this is far out of reach.

Three large consecutive factors.title: Three large consecutive factors
Three large consecutive factors.why: Needs three consecutive integers each n^0.9-almost-prime; beyond Tao-Teraväinen correlation methods, near parity barrier.

A mixed Fermat equation.title: A mixed Fermat equation
A mixed Fermat equation.why: Integral points on a log-general-type surface; no local obstruction found (moduli <400), no small solutions; finiteness needs Vojta-type input.

Squares of seven-free primes.title: Squares of seven-free primes
Squares of seven-free primes.why: Hua five-prime-squares with Maynard digit restriction; quadratic Weyl sums over digit-restricted primes are hard but plausible.

Square-sum 4-cycle factors.title: Square-sum 4-cycle factors
Square-sum 4-cycle factors.why: C4-factor of square-sum graph; likely constructive/absorption, Hamiltonicity already known; moderate combinatorics.

Prime-sum graph and perfect codes.title: Prime-sum graph and perfect codes
Prime-sum graph and perfect codes.why: Perfect codes in bipartite prime-sum graph; closed neighbourhoods ~2n/log n force tiny codes; likely only small n, needs sieve care.

Primes in the {5,8} funnel's tree.title: Primes in the {5,8} funnel's tree
Primes in the {5,8} funnel's tree.why: Positive density of each fate needs distributional control of orbits of P(n)+P(n+1); f(n) small only on density-zero sets.

Packing density of Gerver's sofa.title: Packing density of Gerver's sofa
Packing density of Gerver's sofa.why: Packing density of Gerver's sofa is unknown even numerically; proving transcendence is far beyond methods.

Rotation-proof lattice-point-poor shapes.title: Rotation-proof lattice-point-poor shapes
Rotation-proof lattice-point-poor shapes.why: Second-order term of min-max rotated lattice count runs into Gauss circle problem-type discrepancy; also somewhat vaguely posed.

Ising model on the spectre tiling.title: Ising model on the spectre tiling
Ising model on the spectre tiling.why: Exact beta_c and SLE3 on aperiodic non-isoradial graph; open even for generic periodic graphs; sibling of existing hat Ising items.

Percolation threshold of the square-sum.title: Percolation threshold of the square-sum graph
Percolation threshold of the square-sum.why: Threshold 1/lambda of kernel 1/(2sqrt(x+y)) via inhomogeneous/dense-graph percolation theory; needs local tree-likeness check.

Random greedy square-sum path.title: Random greedy square-sum path
Random greedy square-sum path.why: Random greedy path on deterministic graph of degree ~sqrt N; no differential-equation method directly applies; limit may be 0.

Random digit deletion.title: Random digit deletion
Random digit deletion.why: Heuristically c=1 (harmonic sum of prime chances); rigorous needs higher-moment prime counts on digit-deleted numbers.

Doubled prime map with a 1231 loop.title: Doubled prime map with a 1231 loop
Doubled prime map with a 1231 loop.why: Cycles (93..315) and (1231,2473,6183) confirmed; growth on primes up to 2.5x makes global convergence Collatz-type.

Triple factor map minus two.title: Triple factor map minus two
Triple factor map minus two.why: Fixed points 8, 33 and cycles through 20 (13), 177 (9) confirmed; global convergence is Collatz-type.

Treewidth of the prime-sum graph.title: Treewidth of the prime-sum graph
Treewidth of the prime-sum graph.why: tw<=n via odd vertex cover; mod-3 structure gives C6 blow-up separators so c<1; exact c needs prime sums on dense sets.

Two loops for P(n)+P(n+2).title: Two loops for P(n)+P(n+2)
Two loops for P(n)+P(n+2).why: Collatz-type; f(n)<=2n+2 with twin-prime-like escape chains (n, n+2 both prime) impossible to rule out with current tools.

Three consecutive largest factors.title: Three consecutive largest factors
Three consecutive largest factors.why: Collatz-type largest-prime-factor map; no contraction argument controls rare orbits where P(n),P(n+2) both near n.

Three pairs.title: Three pairs
Three pairs.why: Collatz-type; growth steps need n, 2n+1 both prime (Sophie Germain pairs), uncontrollable.

Every binary block in Gerver's constant.title: Every binary block in Gerver's constant
Every binary block in Gerver's constant.why: Disjunctivity unknown even for sqrt2; Gerver area not even known irrational. Near-variant of existing 'Gerver constant is normal'.

An irrational sum over largest factors.title: An irrational sum over largest factors
An irrational sum over largest factors.why: Irrationality of arithmetic series like this has no known method; same flavour as existing 'Irrational prime weights'.

Smooth p\u00b2+1.title: Smooth p²+1
Smooth p\u00b2+1.why: Heuristically true; known smooth-value results for n²+1 (Dartyge, Harman) fall short of exponent 1/2 at prime arguments.

Large prime factors of 2^n + 3^n.title: Large prime factors of 2^n + 3^n
Large prime factors of 2^n + 3^n.why: Stewart gives only P(a^n-b^n)>n·exp(c log n/loglog n); exponent 2 far beyond current methods.

Sidon sets of seven-free numbers.title: Sidon sets of seven-free numbers
Sidon sets of seven-free numbers.why: Trivial bound sqrt(N); digit-wise constructions give only ~3^k vs sqrt(10^k), so the true order is a real question.

Prime Nim with Pythagorean primes.title: Prime Nim with Pythagorean primes
Prime Nim with Pythagorean primes.why: Variant of existing 'Infinite Prime Nim losses... show they are rare'; multiples of 4 avoid the moves, so no Sárközy shortcut.

The Hamiltonicity game on square sums.title: The Hamiltonicity game on square sums
The Hamiltonicity game on square sums.why: Min degree ~0.41sqrt(N), but Maker-Breaker results need pseudorandomness/expansion of S_N, itself open.

Infinite cube-sum paths.title: Infinite cube-sum paths
Infinite cube-sum paths.why: No obvious colouring counterexample (residue obstructions fail), and the increasing-path requirement blocks König-type arguments.

Stopping times of the doubling map.title: Stopping times of the doubling map
Stopping times of the doubling map.why: Close variant of existing 'Affine prime maps, quantitative' (3p+4); needs iterated P(2p+1) distribution, beyond EH-level. 8-cycle verified.

Moser's worm in the sphere.title: Moser's worm in the sphere
Moser's worm in the sphere.why: Planar Moser worm not even pinned within 1%; spherical version at least as hard.

Cheeger constant of the sofa.title: Cheeger constant of the sofa
Cheeger constant of the sofa.why: Transcendence of a variational constant of a non-convex body; Gerver's area itself not known irrational.

Random sequential prime-sum packing.title: Random sequential prime-sum packing
Random sequential prime-sum packing.why: Bipartite odd/even race; answer likely 1/2 via one parity winning; needs prime equidistribution but seems standard.

Sharp threshold for prime-sum Hamiltonic.title: Sharp threshold for prime-sum Hamiltonicity
Sharp threshold for prime-sum Hamiltonic.why: Degree ~2n/log n gives p ~ log²n/n; requires sieve-based pseudorandomness of codegrees, plausible but technical.

Prime factor plus digit sum.title: Prime factor plus digit sum
Prime factor plus digit sum.why: Non-primes contract; must rule out infinite prime chains p->p+s(p), Cunningham-chain-like and out of reach.

Formal verification depth of RH.title: Formal verification depth of RH
Formal verification depth of RH.why: Instance of Friedman's grand conjecture; likely yes via WKL0 conservativity over IΣ1, but demands reworking the whole proof.

Square subtraction with prime piles.title: Square subtraction with prime piles
Square subtraction with prime piles.why: Subtract-a-square P-positions are sparse and structureless; primes in them is like existing 'Square losses in Prime Nim', hopeless.

Seven-free factorial-like products.title: Seven-free factorial-like products
Seven-free factorial-like products.why: Akin to Erdős's 2^n digit problems; fixed blocks of last nonzero digits (automatic) likely avoid 7 infinitely often.

Largest prime factor of 2^n + n.title: Largest prime factor of 2^n + n
Largest prime factor of 2^n + n.why: Known lower bounds via linear forms in logs are ~log n scale; superlinear in n far beyond.

P(n)+P(n+1)\u22121.title: P(n)+P(n+1)−1
P(n)+P(n+1)\u22121.why: Collatz-type prime-factor dynamics; growth via prime chains p→p+P(p+1)−1, no contraction argument available.

Neighbours' largest factors.title: Neighbours' largest factors
Neighbours' largest factors.why: Twin-prime-type growth (n±1 prime gives 2n); proving finitely many cycles is Collatz-hard.

Last digits of consecutive largest facto.title: Last digits of consecutive largest factors
Last digits of consecutive largest facto.why: Joint residues of P(n),P(n+1) mod 10; only log-density results (Teräväinen-type) known for consecutive P; natural density open.

Prime continued fractions.title: Prime continued fractions
Prime continued fractions.why: Transcendence of a Hausdorff dimension of a CF Cantor set: no known methods even for E_{1,2}.

Prime plus two seven-free squares.title: Prime plus two seven-free squares
Prime plus two seven-free squares.why: Linnik p+x²+y² needed dispersion; adding digit restrictions on x,y requires Maynard-type Fourier input. Plausible but hard.

Infinite monochromatic square-sum paths.title: Infinite monochromatic square-sum paths
Infinite monochromatic square-sum paths.why: Infinite version of existing finite square-sum path Ramsey problem; not obviously trivial, no known reference.

Roth for seven-free numbers.title: Roth for seven-free numbers
Roth for seven-free numbers.why: Relative Roth in digit-restricted set; Fourier structure of missing-digit sets suggests density increment works, unknown in literature.

Partizan Prime Nim.title: Partizan Prime Nim
Partizan Prime Nim.why: Partizan subtraction game with infinite prime sets; claimed switch structure unverified and could fail; exploratory.

Is Prime Nim's losing set definable?.title: Is Prime Nim's losing set definable?
Is Prime Nim's losing set definable?.why: Decidability of (N,+,L) for sparse arithmetic sets tied to prime-pattern conjectures (cf. (N,+,Primes)); likely needs Dickson-type input.

Hamiltonian induced subgraphs of S_N.title: Hamiltonian induced subgraphs of S_N
Hamiltonian induced subgraphs of S_N.why: Needs embedding bounded-degree hard graphs as induced square-sum subgraphs with poly bit size; plausible gadget work.

Prime-sum graph is Hamiltonian-connected.title: Prime-sum graph is Hamiltonian-connected
Prime-sum graph is Hamiltonian-connected.why: Hamiltonian-connected strengthening of prime circle (Greenfield); dense pseudorandom bipartite graph, absorption methods likely suffice.

Unforced blow-up near the forced one.title: Unforced blow-up near the forced one
Unforced blow-up near the forced one.why: Vanishing-forcing blow-up is close to the unforced NS problem; scaling does not trivialize forcing decay.

Prime-digit continued fractions in arith.title: Prime-digit continued fractions in arithmetic progressions
Prime-digit continued fractions in arith.why: Requires periodic CFs with prime quotients (no 1s) in every real quadratic field; McMullen-type arithmetic-chaos problem, all primes allowed eases it.

Hexagonal Lebesgue covering.title: Hexagonal Lebesgue covering
Hexagonal Lebesgue covering.why: Translative universal cover for diameter-1 sets; Lebesgue-type covering, likely mentioned in Brass–Moser–Pach; hard.

Self-avoiding walk on the hat tiling sca.title: Self-avoiding walk on the hat tiling scaling
Self-avoiding walk on the hat tiling sca.why: SAW ν=3/4 is open even on Z²; aperiodic version strictly harder.

Ising with prime couplings.title: Ising with prime couplings
Ising with prime couplings.why: Prime-spaced 1/r² couplings average r²J(r)~1/log r→0; ACCN/Newman–Schulman suggest no transition, claim possibly false.

Stopping time law for P(n)+P(n+1).title: Stopping time law for P(n)+P(n+1)
Stopping time law for P(n)+P(n+1).why: Stopping-time law needs randomness of P(n),P(n+1) along orbits, plus global convergence; Collatz-type (Tao) difficulty.

Neighbour factors plus one.title: Neighbour factors plus one
Neighbour factors plus one.why: Same twin-prime-growth Collatz-type issue as the P(n−1)+P(n+1) map; distinct map, so not duplicate.

Tileability by the spectre is undecidabl.title: Tileability by the spectre is undecidable for regions with holes
Tileability by the spectre is undecidabl.why: Statement fine (title says undecidable, M says NP-complete); gadget reduction for a fixed aperiodic tile plausible.

Sums of a square and a seven-free prime.title: Sums of a square and a seven-free prime
Sums of a square and a seven-free prime.why: Almost-all m²+p with Maynard seven-free primes; needs minor-arc bounds for digit-restricted primes, likely doable.

Largest prime factor of n^n + 1.title: Largest prime factor of n^n + 1
Largest prime factor of n^n + 1.why: Primitive divisors give P≥2n+1; →∞ needs Stewart-type bounds with varying base, beyond current Baker methods.

Doubling the largest factor.title: Doubling the largest factor
Doubling the largest factor.why: Collatz-like; growth via Sophie Germain chains unbounded locally; cycle verified, no proof route.

Three halves of the largest factor.title: Three halves of the largest factor
Three halves of the largest factor.why: Collatz-like 3p/2 growth on primes; no contraction argument; cycle (3,5,8) verified.

Primes with equal binary and ternary dig.title: Primes with equal binary and ternary digit sums
Primes with equal binary and ternary dig.why: Spiegelhofer proved s2=s3 collisions for integers (2021); prime version needs joint two-base Mauduit-Rivat, open.

Linnik\u2013Gallagher with seven-free pr.title: Linnik–Gallagher with seven-free primes
Linnik\u2013Gallagher with seven-free pr.why: Needs Gallagher method with Maynard missing-digit primes; plausible but nontrivial; existing list has related seven-free items.

Tur\u00e1n density of a twisted triple s.title: Turán density of a twisted triple system
Tur\u00e1n density of a twisted triple s.why: F not 3-partite (forces 1,2 same part), so pi(F)>0; specific Turan density likely open, flag-algebra territory.

Bounded orbits for polynomial prime maps.title: Bounded orbits for polynomial prime maps
Bounded orbits for polynomial prime maps.why: Undecidability-type question on prime-factor dynamics; minor issue P(0),P(1) undefined when f(n) in {0,+-1}.

Resolution lower bound for square-sum co.title: Resolution lower bound for square-sum colouring
Resolution lower bound for square-sum co.why: chi(S_N) itself unknown; proof-complexity lower bound for structured number-theoretic graph, hard but well-posed.

Kneser graphs of square sums.title: Kneser graphs of square sums
Kneser graphs of square sums.why: Kneser upper bound N-2k+2 trivial; lower bound via alternation number/topological method likely tractable.

Extremal square-sum subgraphs.title: Extremal square-sum subgraphs
Extremal square-sum subgraphs.why: Upper O(N^{3/2}) trivial; S_N has ~N^2 log N C4s; Sidon subsets of squares give C4-free subgraphs; gap real.

Square-sum orderings avoiding progressio.title: Square-sum orderings avoiding progressions
Square-sum orderings avoiding progressio.why: Base Hamiltonian path problem treated as known; AP-avoidance constraint adds genuine difficulty.

Distance sets of the spectre tiling.title: Distance sets of the spectre tiling
Distance sets of the spectre tiling.why: Centres in finite-rank Z-module; distinct squared distances count via quadratic form values; doable but messy.

Isospectral monotiles.title: Isospectral monotiles
Isospectral monotiles.why: Open-ended construction; isospectrality via transplantation unlikely to fit aperiodic monotiles; very hard either way.

Equal-area hat dissection.title: Equal-area hat dissection
Equal-area hat dissection.why: Minimal dissection lower bounds are notoriously hard to prove; well-defined but likely intractable to certify.

Uniform spanning tree of the square-sum.title: Uniform spanning tree of the square-sum graph
Uniform spanning tree of the square-sum.why: Expected alpha=1/2 via expander UST results (Michaeli-Nachmias-Shalev); needs spectral gap of S_N, itself in existing list.

Hitting probability for 2P(n)+1 random v.title: Hitting probability for 2P(n)+1 random variant
Hitting probability for 2P(n)+1 random v.why: Recurrence needs control of P(2p+-1) distribution, like Elliott-Halberstam-level input; simulations hit 5 often.

The shift-3 prime map.title: The shift-3 prime map
The shift-3 prime map.why: Collatz-like; twin-prime-like pairs n,n+3 make orbits grow; cycles verified to 20000.

Four fates of P(n)+P(n+1)+1.title: Four fates of P(n)+P(n+1)+1
Four fates of P(n)+P(n+1)+1.why: Collatz-like; four fates verified to 20000; no contraction mechanism.

Seven-free square sums of two squares.title: Seven-free square sums of two squares
Seven-free square sums of two squares.why: Heuristically exceptional set infinite (reps r(n) small vs 0.81^digits); proving it still needs constructing explicit families.

Twin width of square-sum graphs.title: Twin width of square-sum graphs
Twin width of square-sum graphs.why: Easy if S_N is K_{t,t}-free (bounded tww + K_tt-free => bounded degeneracy), but K_{t,t} in squares is open.

Clique minors in the prime-sum graph.title: Clique minors in the prime-sum graph
Clique minors in the prime-sum graph.why: n/sqrt(log n) is trivial edge-count upper bound; random heuristic gives n/log n, so claimed lower bound likely false/very hard.
